# TradeNotes business model
**Projections, not actual revenue. Nobody has paid yet.** Per-tier maths and full scenario tables: `docs/subscriptions/SUBSCRIPTION_UNIT_ECONOMICS.md` (generated by `scripts/unit-economics.py`).

## Revenue
Free $0 · Standard $12/mo · Premium $24/mo (USD, monthly only). Founding-member discount not modelled (no mechanism yet).

## Costs
| Type | Item | Monthly |
|---|---|---|
| Payment processing (variable) | HandyPay 4.9% + $0.40 | $0.99 per Standard, $1.58 per Premium |
| Hosting | Vercel Pro | $20 |
| Database | Supabase Pro (dedicated) | $25 (estimate) |
| Email | Resend | $0 → $20 above ~3,000 emails/mo |
| Domain | tradenotes.dev | ~$1.10 |
| Monitoring | Sentry | $0 → $26 at scale |
| Other variable | storage/compute per user | $0.01–0.03 |
| **Fixed operating at launch** | | **≈ $46** |
| One-off | legal review $300–1,500; DPA registration (fee unverified); business registration $50–300 | |
| Marketing | Instagram test | $50 once |

## Contribution
Standard $10.99 (91.6%) · Premium $22.39 (93.3%) · blended 70/30 ≈ **$14.41 per payer**.

## Break-even
- Platform costs ($46/mo): **4 paying subscribers**.
- Plus amortising a $1,000 legal/setup spend over 12 months (~$83/mo): **≈ 9 payers**.
- Plus a $500/mo ad budget later: **≈ 44 payers**.

## Growth scenarios (registered users; Base mix 85% Free / 11% Standard / 4% Premium)
| Registered users | Paying | MRR | Monthly result after fees + platform |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 10 | 1 | $12 | −$35 |
| 50 | 8 | $120 | +$64 |
| 100 | 15 | $228 | +$164 |
| 500 | 75 | $1,140 | +$1,002 |
| 1,000 | 150 | $2,280 | +$2,030 |
| 5,000 | 750 | $11,400 | +$10,345 |
Conservative and optimistic mixes, and the "all counts are payers" view, are in the unit-economics file. Excluded everywhere: founder time, taxes, refunds/chargebacks, ads.

## What the model says
1. Delivery cost is not the problem; **acquisition and conversion are.** Watch: sign-up → 5 trades logged (activation) → paid.
2. A 15% paid share (Base) is ambitious for freemium; plan around Conservative (8%) until real data exists.
3. Premium needs Premium-only value before it carries weight; until then expect most payers on Standard.
4. Market data for backtesting ($50–200+/mo) is affordable only after ~5–10 Premium subscribers.
